::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[How do I declare an option that takes an input value?](https://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/5279/how-do-i-declare-an-option-that-takes-an-input-value), asked by [Tomas Aschan](https://tex.stackexchange.com/users/223/tomas-aschan) on TeX Stack Exchange (2010-11-12; [CC BY-SA 2.5](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/2.5/)):

> I know I can declare and execute an option for my package using
>
> ```latex
> \DeclareOption{myoption}{\typeout{I did it!}}
> \ProcessOptions
> ```
>
> but now I'd like to give the option a value:
>
> ```latex
> \DeclareOption{type}{\typeout{You typed: \CurrentOptionValue}}
> ```
>
> which would be used as follows:
>
> ```latex
> \usepackage[type="hello, world!"]{mypackage}
> ```
>
> Requirements on the value string is that it can contain at least some nonalphanumeric characters, like spaces, commas and dots (and maybe some others...).
:::

The [xkeyval](http://tug.ctan.org/cgi-bin/ctanPackageInformation.py?id=xkeyval) package is your friend.
